Test image: A mango leaf with a grayish-white powdery/dusty coating covering the entire upper surface. The leaf looks dull, with diffuse pale patches — no brown necrotic spots, no dark sooty coating, no tip dieback. This strongly suggests Powdery Mildew.

Now let me view one reference from each class before revisiting.
Excellent match — same diffuse pale powdery patches on a green leaf surface. Now one from Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows yellowed/browned leaf with lesions — very different from the test image. Now Die_Back.
Die_Back shows severely desiccated, brown dead leaf — very different. Now Sooty_Mould.

Sooty Mould shows dark black/gray speckled patches — darker and more spotted than the test image. The test image has lighter, more uniformly diffuse white-gray coverage. Powdery Mildew remains the top candidate. Let me view more Powdery Mildew references to confirm.
Strong match — same diffuse pale whitish patches. Let me continue through the budget.
I've viewed all 12 unique references. Need 3 more views to reach the budget of 16. Re-examining key comparisons:

All 16 views complete. Summary:

- **Powdery_Mildew** references: diffuse pale white/gray powdery patches on green leaf — **identical** to the test image in color, texture, and pattern.
- **Sooty_Mould**: dark black/olive-green speckled patches, clearly darker and more spotty.
- **Anthracnose**: discrete dark brown necrotic lesions on green leaf.
- **Die_Back**: completely desiccated brown/tan dead leaf tissue.

The test image matches Powdery_Mildew across all three reference images with high confidence.
